https://www.fox16.com/news/jacksonville-man-sentenced-to-15-year-prison-term-in-power-grid-attacks/

LITTLE ROCK, AR – A Jacksonville man has been sentenced to 15 years in prison for attacks on power grids in Central Arkansas between August and October 2013.

Jason Woodring, 38, had been accused of causing millions of dollars worth of damage. His attacks included sabotaging an electrical support tower and downing a 500,000-volt power line onto a railroad track near Cabot; setting fire to and destroying an Extra High Voltage (EHV) switching station in Scott; and cutting down two power poles, which led to the temporary loss of power to about 9,000 customers in Jacksonville.

In addition to the term of imprisonment, Woodring will be required to pay $4,792,224.06 in restitution to Entergy for the attacks near Cabot and in Scott. He will also have to pay $48,729.39 to First Electric Cooperative for the damage in Jacksonville.

Woodring was charged in an eight-count indictment by a federal grand jury on November 6, 2013. On March 10, 2015, Woodring pleaded guilty to counts 2, 3, 4, and 8 of the indictment, including destruction of an energy facility for downing the Cabot power lines (Count Two) and for setting fire to the Scott power station (Count Three). He also pleaded guilty to using fire to commit a felony (Count Four) in relation to the arson in Scott. Finally, Woodring pleaded guilty to being an illegal drug user in possession of various firearms and ammunition (Count Eight) and agreed to forfeit the firearms and ammunition.

On Thursday, United States District Judge Billy Roy Wilson accepted a plea agreement and imposed the recommended 15-year sentence.

There is no parole in the federal system. Upon his release from prison Woodring must serve five years of supervised release.

This investigation was conducted by the FBI, Joint Terrorism Task Force, ATF, Union Pacific Police, Entergy, First Electric, Lonoke County Sheriff’s Office, Cabot Police, Arkansas State Police, Conway Police Department, Little Rock Police Department and Arkansas Game and Fish Commission.
